title.zh: 卷二十三 志第十三 樂下
title.raw: 卷二十三 志第十三 樂下 Volume 23 Treatises 13: Music Part Two

sentences.zh: 樂志下

translations.literal: Treatise on Music, Part Two
translations.idiomatic: Treatise on Music, Part Two

sentences.zh: 永嘉之亂，海內分崩，伶官樂器，皆沒于劉、石。

translations.literal: In the Yongjia upheaval, the realm within the seas broke apart; court musicians and their instruments all fell into the possession of Liu [Yuan] and Shi [Le].
translations.idiomatic: When Yongjia-era chaos tore the empire apart, palace musicians and their instruments passed entirely into the hands of Liu Yuan's and Shi Le's regimes.

sentences.zh: 江左初立宗廟，尚書下太常祭祀所用樂名。

translations.literal: When the ancestral shrines were first established south of the Yangzi, the Secretariat forwarded to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices an inquiry concerning the names of the music used in sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After the court first set up its ancestral temples in the south, the Secretariat asked the Minister of Imperial Sacrifices what the ritual music was called.

sentences.zh: 太常賀循答云：「魏氏增損漢樂，以為一代之禮，未審大晉樂名所以為異。

translations.literal: He Xun, Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, replied: "The Wei dynasty revised Han music to constitute ritual for their age; I have not yet examined why the Great Jin's musical nomenclature should differ from it.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices answered: "Wei adapted Han ritual music for its own dynastic rites; I am not certain what distinguishes Great Jin's musical titles."

sentences.zh: 遭離喪亂，舊典不存。

translations.literal: Having undergone bereavement and turmoil, the old canonical precedents no longer survive.
translations.idiomatic: War and exile destroyed the old precedents, and little of the canon survived.

sentences.zh: 然此諸樂皆和之以鐘律，文之以五聲，詠之於歌辭，陳之於舞列。

translations.literal: Yet all these kinds of music were reconciled with bells and pitch-pipes, patterned according to the five tones, sung through lyrics, and arrayed in dance formations.
translations.idiomatic: Yet each piece was tuned to bells and pitch-pipes, structured in the five musical modes, carried by sung texts, and embodied in choreographed dance.

sentences.zh: 宮懸在庭，琴瑟在堂，八音迭奏，雅樂並作，登歌下管，各有常詠，周人之舊也。

translations.literal: Suspended bells stood in the courtyard; zithers and lutes resided in the hall; the eight categories of instruments sounded in alternation, ya music rose together, ascending hymns and wind accompaniment each followed fixed verses—the ancient practice of the Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Half-moon chimes hung in the courtyard, qin and se on the dais, the eight instrument families alternating in concert—court music and ya ensemble together, antiphonal song above and wind below—each with its prescribed lyrics: the Zhou legacy.

sentences.zh: 自漢氏以來，依仿此禮，自造新詩而已。

translations.literal: Since the Han dynasty, courts have broadly followed this ritual pattern, composing new lyrics of their own.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han times, courts have kept to that framework while supplying fresh lyrics.

sentences.zh: 舊京荒廢，今既散亡，音韻曲折，又無識者，則於今難以意言。

translations.literal: The former capital lies ruined and abandoned; now that [those traditions] are scattered and lost, and no one understands the turns of melody and tone, it is difficult today to speak of them with assurance.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang lies in ruins, and with musicians and scores gone, no one today can recover the actual pitches and turns of phrase—it is almost impossible to reconstruct them from guesswork.

sentences.zh: 」于時以無雅樂器及伶人，省太樂並鼓吹令。

translations.literal: " At that time, because there were neither ritual instruments nor musicians, the Grand Music Bureau was abolished along with the office of the Wind-and-Drum Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, lacking proper instruments and performers, the court cut the Grand Music Bureau and the office that supervised wind and drums.

sentences.zh: 是後頗得登歌，食舉之樂，猶有未備。

translations.literal: Afterward they gradually recovered music for the ascending hymn and for feasts, yet much still remained incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: Later they recovered something of the ascending hymn and banquet music, but the restoration was still patchy.

sentences.zh: 太寧末，明帝又訪阮孚等增益之。

translations.literal: Near the end of the Taining reign, Emperor Ming again consulted Ruan Fu and others to augment it.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Taining era, Emperor Ming once more sent for Ruan Fu and others to expand the repertoire.

sentences.zh: 咸和中，成帝乃復置太樂官，鳩集遺逸，而尚未有金石也。

translations.literal: In the Xianhe era, Emperor Cheng restored the Grand Music office, gathered what had survived, but still possessed no bronze or stone chimes.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianhe, Emperor Cheng re-established the Grand Music directorate and collected scattered pieces, but still had no metal or stone percussion.

sentences.zh: 庾亮為荊州，與謝尚修復雅樂，未具而亮薨。

translations.literal: Yu Liang, as governor of Jingzhou, together with Xie Shang worked to restore ya music; before the task was finished Yu Liang died.
translations.idiomatic: While Yu Liang governed Jingzhou he joined Xie Shang in rebuilding ya music, but died before the work was done.

sentences.zh: 庾翼、桓溫專事軍旅，樂器在庫，遂至朽壞焉。

translations.literal: Yu Yi and Huan Wen gave themselves wholly to military affairs; the instruments stayed in the armory until they rotted away.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi and Huan Wen focused on war; instruments mouldered in storehouses.

sentences.zh: 及慕容亻雋平冉閔，兵戈之際，而鄴下樂人亦頗有來者。

translations.literal: When Murong Jun defeated Ran Min, even amid the clash of arms quite a few musicians from Ye came south.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Jun overthrew Ran Min, a fair number of Ye musicians drifted south despite the fighting.

sentences.zh: 永和十一年，謝尚鎮壽陽，於是采拾樂人，以備太樂，並制石磬，雅樂始頗具。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yonghe, Xie Shang was stationed at Shouyang; thereupon he collected musicians to supply the Grand Music, and had stone chimes fashioned—ya music then began to be somewhat complete.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghe 11, with Xie Shang holding Shouyang, he rounded up performers for the Grand Music and commissioned stone chimes—ya music at last began to look like a real orchestra.

sentences.zh: 面王猛平鄴，慕容氏所得樂聲又入關右。

translations.literal: When Wang Meng took Ye, the musical attainments the Murong clan had acquired also entered Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Meng conquered Ye, the musical heritage the Murong had collected followed the armies into the Guanzhong heartland.

sentences.zh: 太元中，破苻堅，又獲其樂工楊蜀等，閑習舊樂，於是四廂金石始備焉。

translations.literal: In the Taiyuan era, after defeating Fu Jian, they also captured his musicians such as Yang Shu, versed in the old music; only then were the four-sided bronze and stone ensembles finally complete.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiyuan years, victory over Fu Jian yielded professionals such as Yang Shu who knew the classical repertoire, and for the first time the four-sided layout of bells and chimes was complete.

sentences.zh: 乃使曹毗、王珣等增造宗廟歌詩，然郊祀遂不設樂。

translations.literal: Thereupon they had Cao Pi, Wang Xun, and others compose additional hymns for the ancestral temple; yet suburban sacrifices still went without music.
translations.idiomatic: The court then commissioned Cao Pi, Wang Xun, and others to draft new temple hymns, though suburban offerings still had no music.

sentences.zh: 今列其詞於後雲。

translations.literal: Their texts are listed below.
translations.idiomatic: The lyrics are set out below.

sentences.zh: 歌宣帝曹毗

translations.literal: Hymn to Emperor Xuan (by Cao Pi)
translations.idiomatic: Hymn to Emperor Xuan — Cao Pi

sentences.zh: 于赫高祖，德協靈符。

translations.literal: Ah, majestic High Ancestor—his virtue matched the numinous tally.
translations.idiomatic: Radiant High Ancestor, whose virtue answered heaven's token.

sentences.zh: 應運撥亂，厘整天衢。

translations.literal: He answered the age's call, quelled chaos, and put the great highways in order.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the mandate, crushed rebellion, and cleared the imperial roads.

sentences.zh: 勳格宇宙，化動八區。

translations.literal: His merit spans the cosmos; his transforming influence stirs the eight directions.
translations.idiomatic: His achievement fills heaven and earth; his transforming power stirs every quarter.

sentences.zh: 肅以典刑，陶以玄珠。

translations.literal: With solemn statutes he shaped them; with the dark pearl he molded them.
translations.idiomatic: He framed them with canonical law; he shaped them with the pearl of mystery.

sentences.zh: 神石吐瑞，靈芝自敷。

translations.literal: Spirit stones spat auspicious omens; lingzhi mushrooms spread of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Marvel-stones spat omens; lingzhi sprouted unbidden.

sentences.zh: 肇基天命，道均唐虞。

translations.literal: He founded the mandate of Heaven; his Way equals [those of] Tang and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He laid heaven's foundation; his Way stands beside Tang and Yu.

sentences.zh: 歌景帝曹毗

translations.literal: Hymn to Emperor Jing (by Cao Pi)
translations.idiomatic: Hymn to Emperor Jing — Cao Pi

sentences.zh: 景皇承運，纂隆洪緒。

translations.literal: The Brilliant Emperor received the succession and enlarged the mighty enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: The Brilliant Emperor took up the line and magnified the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 皇羅重抗，天暉再舉。

translations.literal: The imperial net was raised anew; heaven's radiance shone forth again.
translations.idiomatic: The royal net flew again; celestial radiance returned.

sentences.zh: 蠢矣二寇，擾我揚楚。

translations.literal: How reckless those two bandits, troubling our Yang and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Those two marauders threw Yang and Chu into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 乃整元戎，以膏齊斧。

translations.literal: Then he marshaled the hosts of war to oil the battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: He drew up the grand army and whetted the executioner's axe.

sentences.zh: 亹亹神算，赫赫王旅。

translations.literal: Tireless his divine strategies; splendid his royal armies.
translations.idiomatic: Divine plans without cease; royal hosts in splendor.

sentences.zh: 鯨鯢既平，功冠帝宇。

translations.literal: Once the great whales were laid low, his merit crowned the imperial realm.
translations.idiomatic: When the leviathans were destroyed, his merit crowned the throne.

sentences.zh: 歌文帝曹毗

translations.literal: Hymn to Emperor Wen (by Cao Pi)
translations.idiomatic: Hymn to Emperor Wen — Cao Pi

sentences.zh: 太祖齊聖，王猷誕融。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor, consummate sage—kingly designs vast and melting.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor, all-perfect sage—his royal pattern flows wide and deep.

sentences.zh: 仁教四塞，天基累崇。

translations.literal: Humanizing rule reached the four quarters; heaven's foundation rose tier on tier.
translations.idiomatic: Humanizing teaching filled the four quarters; heaven's base mounted ever higher.

sentences.zh: 皇室多難，嚴清紫宮。

translations.literal: The house faced many trials; he purified the Purple Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The house endured repeated crises; he cleansed the Purple Palace.

sentences.zh: 威厲秋霜，惠過春風。

translations.literal: Stern as autumn frost in awe; kindly as spring wind in grace.
translations.idiomatic: His awe is autumn frost; his kindness exceeds spring wind.

sentences.zh: 平蜀夷楚，以文以戎。

translations.literal: He pacified Shu and subdued Chu—by civil virtue and by arms.
translations.idiomatic: He stilled Shu and broke Chu—by culture and by arms.

sentences.zh: 奄有參墟，聲流無窮。

translations.literal: He embraced the lands around Shen; his fame flows without end.
translations.idiomatic: He held the heartland east of Shen; his fame knows no end.

sentences.zh: 歌武帝曹毗

translations.literal: Hymn to Emperor Wu (by Cao Pi)
translations.idiomatic: Hymn to Emperor Wu — Cao Pi

sentences.zh: 于穆武皇，允龔欽明。

translations.literal: Oh, august Martial Sovereign—truly reverent, truly luminous.
translations.idiomatic: Oh, august Martial Sovereign—supremely reverent, supremely bright.

sentences.zh: 應期登禪，龍飛紫庭。

translations.literal: At the appointed season he ascended the abdication throne; the dragon flew within the purple court.
translations.idiomatic: When the hour came he mounted the abdicated throne; the dragon soared within the purple precincts.

sentences.zh: 百揆時序，聽斷以情。

translations.literal: All offices kept their seasons; in judgment he listened to human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred duties ran in season; in deciding cases he heeded human hearts.

sentences.zh: 殊域既賓，偽吳亦平。

translations.literal: Alien lands became guests; false Wu too was brought to peace.
translations.idiomatic: Distant lands tendered allegiance; counterfeit Wu was likewise pacified.

sentences.zh: 晨流甘露，宵映朗星。

translations.literal: Morning dew flowed sweet as nectar; night skies shone with lucid stars.
translations.idiomatic: Morning brought sweet dew; night skies gleamed with steady stars.

sentences.zh: 野有擊壤，路垂頌聲。

translations.literal: In the fields men played [the ball-toss game]; along the roads praise hung in the air.
translations.idiomatic: In the fields folk struck the earth-ball game; along every road songs of praise.

sentences.zh: 歌元帝曹毗

translations.literal: Hymn to Emperor Yuan (by Cao Pi)
translations.idiomatic: Hymn to Emperor Yuan — Cao Pi

sentences.zh: 運屯百六，天羅解貫。

translations.literal: When fortune ran its evil span of 'one hundred and six,' heaven's net slackened and broke.
translations.idiomatic: When fate reached the ill cycle of one hundred six, heaven's net loosened and snapped.

sentences.zh: 元皇勃興，網籠江漢。

translations.literal: The Original Emperor rose in vigor, casting his net over the Jiang and Han.
translations.idiomatic: The Original Emperor rose with force and spread his rule across the Jiang and Han.

sentences.zh: 仰齊七政，俯平禍亂。

translations.literal: He aligned himself with the seven regulators above and settled calamity and chaos below.
translations.idiomatic: Above he aligned the seven celestial powers; below he stilled disaster and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 化若風行，澤猶雨散。

translations.literal: His transforming influence swept like the wind; his bounty scattered like rain.
translations.idiomatic: His transforming influence swept like wind; his bounty fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 淪光更曜，金輝復煥。

translations.literal: Submerged radiance shone anew; golden gleam blazed bright once more.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden brilliance flared anew; golden glory burned bright again.

sentences.zh: 德冠千載，蔚有餘粲。

translations.literal: Virtue surpassed a thousand ages; lush glory yet remained.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue towers over a thousand ages; glorious surplus still abounds.

sentences.zh: 歌明帝曹毗

translations.literal: Hymn to Emperor Ming (by Cao Pi)
translations.idiomatic: Hymn to Emperor Ming — Cao Pi

sentences.zh: 明明肅祖，闡弘帝祚。

translations.literal: Bright indeed the Revered Ancestor—he enlarged the imperial succession.
translations.idiomatic: Bright indeed the Revered Ancestor—he widened the imperial inheritance.

sentences.zh: 英風夙發，清暉載路。

translations.literal: Heroic breath stirred early; clear radiance lit the road.
translations.idiomatic: Heroic spirit stirred at dawn; pure splendor lit the road.

sentences.zh: 奸逆縱忒，罔式皇度。

translations.literal: Treacherous rebels ran wild, spurning the royal norm.
translations.idiomatic: The traitors ran riot, scorning the royal measure.

sentences.zh: 躬振硃旗，遂豁天步。

translations.literal: Himself he raised the crimson banner and so cleared heaven's course.
translations.idiomatic: He personally raised the scarlet standard and opened heaven's road.

sentences.zh: 宏猷允塞，高羅雲布。

translations.literal: Grand designs filled every corner; high nets spread like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Great plans filled the realm; lofty nets spread like clouds.

sentences.zh: 品物咸甯，洪基永固。

translations.literal: All things found peace; the mighty foundation stood forever firm.
translations.idiomatic: All creation rested secure; the great foundation stood unshakable.

sentences.zh: 歌成帝曹毗

translations.literal: Hymn to Emperor Cheng (by Cao Pi)
translations.idiomatic: Hymn to Emperor Cheng — Cao Pi

sentences.zh: 于休顯宗，道澤玄播。

translations.literal: Oh, splendid Manifest Ancestor—his Way and dew spread far in silence.
translations.idiomatic: Oh, splendid Manifest Ancestor—his virtue and grace spread silently far.

sentences.zh: 式宣德音，暢物以和。

translations.literal: He voiced the virtue-tones of rule and tuned all things to harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He sounded the moral tones of governance and tuned the myriad things to harmony.

sentences.zh: 邁德蹈仁，匪禮不過。

translations.literal: He walked in mercy and benevolence and broke no ritual bond.
translations.idiomatic: He trod the path of kindness and humaneness and never broke ritual bounds.

sentences.zh: 敷以純風，濯以清波。

translations.literal: With pure influence he washed them; with limpid waves he cleansed them.
translations.idiomatic: With pristine influence he rinsed them; with limpid waves he bathed them.

sentences.zh: 連理映阜，鳴鳳棲柯。

translations.literal: Paired trunks crowned the mound; singing phoenixes rested on the bough.
translations.idiomatic: Twin trunks crowned the mound; phoenixes sang in the branches.

sentences.zh: 同規放勳，義蓋山河。

translations.literal: He matched the model of Fangxun; righteousness covered hill and stream.
translations.idiomatic: He rivaled the model of Fangxun; righteousness mantled mountains and streams.

sentences.zh: 歌康帝曹毗

translations.literal: Hymn to Emperor Kang (by Cao Pi)
translations.idiomatic: Hymn to Emperor Kang — Cao Pi

sentences.zh: 康皇穆穆，仰嗣洪德。

translations.literal: Majestic was Emperor Kang, inheriting the vast virtue.
translations.idiomatic: August Emperor Kang, heir to boundless virtue.

sentences.zh: 為而不宰，雅音四塞。

translations.literal: He acted yet did not domineer; proper tones filled the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He acted without lording over others; right music filled the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 閑邪以誠，鎮物以默。

translations.literal: With quiet vigilance he barred evil; with silence he steadied the realm.
translations.idiomatic: With wary stillness he barred evil; with quietude he steadied the realm.

sentences.zh: 威靜區宇，道宣邦國。

translations.literal: Awe stilled the realm; his Way proclaimed the lands within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: His majesty stilled the realm; his Way spread through the heartland.

sentences.zh: 歌穆帝曹毗

translations.literal: Hymn to Emperor Mu (by Cao Pi)
translations.idiomatic: Hymn to Emperor Mu — Cao Pi

sentences.zh: 孝宗夙哲，休音久臧。

translations.literal: Filial-pious and wise from youth, his fair renown lay long concealed.
translations.idiomatic: Filial and wise from youth, his fine renown long lay hidden.

sentences.zh: 如彼晨離，耀景扶桑。

translations.literal: Like that morning splendor [the sun], its gleam rose over Fusang.
translations.idiomatic: Like the morning radiance, its light climbs over Fusang.

sentences.zh: 垂訓華幄，流潤八荒。

translations.literal: His lessons streamed from the patterned canopy; his moisture soaked the eight wilds.
translations.idiomatic: His teaching flowed from the patterned canopy; his moisture soaked the eight wilds.

sentences.zh: 幽贊玄妙，爰該典章。

translations.literal: Silently he aided the subtle mysteries and embraced the full canon.
translations.idiomatic: Silently he assisted the hidden Way and mastered every canonical pattern.

sentences.zh: 西平僭蜀，北靜舊疆。

translations.literal: He pacified the rebel Shu in the west and quieted the old frontiers in the north.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the rogue Shu westward and stilled the northern marches.

sentences.zh: 高猷遠暢，朝有遺芳。

translations.literal: Lofty designs ranged far; at court his fragrance lingered.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty purpose reached far; sweet fragrance lingered at court.

sentences.zh: 歌哀帝曹毗

translations.literal: Hymn to Emperor Ai (by Cao Pi)
translations.idiomatic: Hymn to Emperor Ai — Cao Pi

sentences.zh: 于穆哀皇，聖心虛遠。

translations.literal: Oh, solemn Emperor Ai—his sacred mind soared remote.
translations.idiomatic: Oh, solemn Emperor Ai—his divine mind dwelt far aloof.

sentences.zh: 雅好玄古，大庭是踐。

translations.literal: He cherished antiquity in simplicity and trod the path of the Great Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He loved high antiquity in simplicity and walked the way of the Grand Hall.

sentences.zh: 道尚無為，治存易簡。

translations.literal: His Way esteemed non-action; his rule aimed at ease and plainness.
translations.idiomatic: His Way honored non-action; his governance valued ease and simplicity.

sentences.zh: 化若風行，時猶草偃。

translations.literal: His transforming touch moved like wind; the age bent like grass before it.
translations.idiomatic: His transforming influence moved like wind; the age bowed like grass.

sentences.zh: 雖曰登遐，徽音彌闡。

translations.literal: Though men say he "ascended afar," his fine tones ring clearer still.
translations.idiomatic: Though people say he journeyed far aloft, his subtle voice rings clearer still.

sentences.zh: 愔愔《雲》《韶》，盡美盡善。

translations.literal: Gentle and gentle the Cloud and Shao pieces—utter beauty, utter goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Softly, softly, the Cloud and Shao airs—beauty absolute, goodness absolute.

sentences.zh: 歌簡文帝王珣

translations.literal: Hymn to Emperor Jianwen (by Wang Xun)
translations.idiomatic: Hymn to Emperor Jianwen — Wang Xun

sentences.zh: 皇矣簡文，于昭於天。

translations.literal: Great indeed Jianwen—his brightness reaches heaven.
translations.idiomatic: How great Jianwen—his radiance reaches to heaven.

sentences.zh: 靈明若神，周淡如川。

translations.literal: Spirit-like insight, godlike; placid depth, river-wide.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit-like in clarity, placid as a great river.

sentences.zh: 沖應其來，實與其遷。

translations.literal: The yielding answered what came; substance shifted with the turning age.
translations.idiomatic: The receptive matched whatever came; essence shifted with the changing times.

sentences.zh: 亹亹心化，日用不言。

translations.literal: Tirelessly his heart transformed all; daily practice needed no words.
translations.idiomatic: Endlessly his heart transformed things; in daily life he used no lectures.

sentences.zh: 易而有親，簡而可傳。

translations.literal: Easy, yet kin drew near; simple, yet fit to hand down.
translations.idiomatic: Easy, yet the close drew near; simple, yet worthy to transmit.

sentences.zh: 觀流彌遠，求本逾玄。

translations.literal: Watch the stream—it runs ever farther; seek the root—it grows more profound.
translations.idiomatic: Follow the current—it runs ever farther; seek the root—it grows deeper still.

sentences.zh: 歌孝武帝王珣

translations.literal: Hymn to Emperor Xiaowu (by Wang Xun)
translations.idiomatic: Hymn to Emperor Xiaowu — Wang Xun

sentences.zh: 天監有晉，欽哉烈宗。

translations.literal: Heaven oversees Jin—revere our fiery Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven looks down on Jin—honor our blazing Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 同規文考，玄默允恭。

translations.literal: He matched the pattern of Wen the Cultured; stillness and modest concord.
translations.idiomatic: He matched King Wen's pattern—silent, humble harmony.

sentences.zh: 威而不猛，約而能通。

translations.literal: Awesome yet never cruel; restrained yet reaching everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Majestic yet never harsh; economical yet inclusive.

sentences.zh: 神鉦一震，九域來同。

translations.literal: The divine gong once trembles; the nine domains come as one.
translations.idiomatic: When the sacred bell-clash rolls out once, the nine regions rally as one.

sentences.zh: 道積淮海，雅頌自東。

translations.literal: The Way piles deep by Huai and sea; ya hymns and eulogies arrive from the east.
translations.idiomatic: His virtue stacks high beside Huai and sea; court hymns arrive from the eastern lands.

sentences.zh: 氣陶醇露，化協時雍。

translations.literal: Breath molds the rich dew; transforming accord matches the age's harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Its breath tempers the mellow dew; harmony fits the halcyon season.

sentences.zh: 四時祠祀曹毗

translations.literal: Four Seasons Sacrifices by Cao Pi
translations.idiomatic: Four Seasons Sacrifices — Cao Pi

sentences.zh: 肅肅清廟，巍巍聖功。

translations.literal: Solemn the pure shrine; lofty the sagely achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn stands the bright shrine; august the holy merit.

sentences.zh: 萬國來賓，禮儀有容。

translations.literal: Ten thousand lands send tribute guests; formal deportment shows composed bearing.
translations.idiomatic: All realms arrive as guests; every ritual gesture keeps measure.

sentences.zh: 鐘鼓振，金石熙。

translations.literal: Drums and bells vibrate; bronze and stone shine forth.
translations.idiomatic: Drums and bells resound; bronze and stone flash bright.

sentences.zh: 宣兆祚，武開基。

translations.literal: August omens spread fortune; martial power lays the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Sacred portents open blessing; martial prowess begins the line.

sentences.zh: 神斯樂兮！

translations.literal: On this the spirits rejoice!
translations.idiomatic: The spirits take joy in this!

sentences.zh: 理管弦，有來斯和。

translations.literal: He sets pipes and strings in order; those who arrive blend in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He arrays winds and strings; all who come join the chorus.

sentences.zh: 說功德，吐清歌。

translations.literal: They expound merit and grace; they pour forth pure songs.
translations.idiomatic: They trumpet deeds and power; they lift unstained song.

sentences.zh: 神斯樂兮！

translations.literal: On this the spirits rejoice!
translations.idiomatic: The spirits take joy in this!

sentences.zh: 洋洋玄化，潤被九壤。

translations.literal: Vast the dark transforming influence; soaking grace drenches the nine soils.
translations.idiomatic: Far-flowing the subtle transformation; its moisture bathes the ninefold earth.

sentences.zh: 民無不悅，道無不往。

translations.literal: Among the people none fail to rejoice; of the Way none fail to follow.
translations.idiomatic: No commoner who does not delight; no course of the Way that is not traveled.

sentences.zh: 禮有儀，樂有式。

translations.literal: Rites keep their pattern; music keeps its form.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremony knows its measure; music knows its mold.

sentences.zh: 詠九功，永無極。

translations.literal: They chant the nine accomplishments—bounds without end.
translations.idiomatic: They sing the nine labors of rule—an end that never comes.

sentences.zh: 神斯樂兮！

translations.literal: On this the spirits rejoice!
translations.idiomatic: The spirits take joy in this!

sentences.zh: 漢時有《短簫鐃歌》之樂，其曲有《硃鷺》、《思悲翁》、《艾如張》、《上之回》、《雍離》、《戰城南》、《巫山高》、《上陵》、《將進酒》、《君馬黃》、《芳樹》、《有所思》、《雉子班》、《聖人出》、《上邪》、《臨高臺》、《遠如期》、《石留》、《務成》、《玄雲》、《黃爵行》《釣竿》等曲，列於鼓吹，多序戰陣之事。

translations.literal: Under Han there existed the music 《Short Panpipes and Naos Songs》; its melodies included 《Red Egret》, 《Thinking of the Old Man》, 《Spreading Mugwort Like a Net》, 《Ascending to the Turn》, 《Yong Leaves Part》, 《South of the City We Fight》, 《Mount Wu Is High》, 《Ascending the Mausoleum》, 《Wine, Advance!》, 《Your Horse Is Yellow》, 《Fragrant Trees》, 《I Had Someone in Mind》, 《Pheasant Broods》, 《The Sage Appears》, 《Oh Heaven Above》, 《From the High Terrace》, 《Far as the Promised Day》, 《Stone Stays》, 《Accomplishing Completion》, 《Dark Clouds》, 《Yellow Sparrow March》《Fishing Rod》, and other tunes, listed among the wind-and-drum suite, most narrating matters of battle formations.
translations.idiomatic: The Han court kept the suite 《Short Reeds and Nao Songs》, with pieces from 《The Vermilion Heron》 through 《The Fishing Rod》, catalogued under military wind-and-drum music and mostly chronicling campaigns.

sentences.zh: 及魏受命，改其十二曲，使繆襲為詞，述以功德代漢。

translations.literal: When Wei received the mandate, they revised twelve of those melodies and had Mi Xi compose lyrics recounting how merit and virtue supplanted Han.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wei inherited heaven's charge, it rewrote twelve titles and commissioned Mi Xi to versify Wei virtue replacing Han.

sentences.zh: 改《硃鷺》為《楚之平》，言魏也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Red Egret》 to 《Chu's Pacification》, referring to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: 《Red Egret》 became 《Pacifying Chu》, speaking for Wei.

sentences.zh: 改《思悲翁》為《戰滎陽》，言曹公也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Thinking of the Old Man》 to 《Battle of Xingyang》, referring to Lord Cao.
translations.idiomatic: 《Thinking of the Old Man》 became 《The Fight at Xingyang》, celebrating Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 改《艾如張》為《獲呂布》，言曹公東圍臨淮，擒呂布也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Spreading Mugwort Like a Net》 to 《Capturing Lü Bu》, referring to Lord Cao's eastern siege of Linhuai and capture of Lü Bu.
translations.idiomatic: 《Spreading Mugwort》 turned into 《Capturing Lü Bu》, marking Cao Cao's eastern tightening of the siege at Linhuai and his seizure of Lü Bu.

sentences.zh: 改《上之回》為《克官渡》，言曹公與袁紹戰，破之於官渡也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Ascending to the Turn》 to 《Taking Guandu》, referring to Lord Cao's war with Yuan Shao and destroying him at Guandu.
translations.idiomatic: 《Ascending to the Turn》 became 《Victory at Guandu》, noting Cao Cao's rout of Yuan Shao at the Guandu ford.

sentences.zh: 改《雍離》為《舊邦》，言曹公勝袁紹於官渡，還譙收藏死亡士卒也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Yong Leaves Part》 to 《The Old Domain》, referring to Lord Cao's victory over Yuan Shao at Guandu, returning to Qiao to gather and bury the dead soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: 《Yong Leaves Part》 was renamed 《The Old Domain》, commemorating Cao Cao's Guandu triumph and his return to Qiao to inter the fallen.

sentences.zh: 改《戰城南》為《定武功》，言曹公初破鄴，武功之定始乎此也。

translations.literal: They changed 《South of the City We Fight》 to 《Settling Martial Prowess》, referring to when Lord Cao first broke Ye and the fixing of martial prowess began then.
translations.idiomatic: 《South of the City We Fight》 became 《Affirming Martial Might》, for Cao Cao's first reduction of Ye, where his military order truly began.

sentences.zh: 改《巫山高》為《屠柳城》，言曹公越北塞，曆白檀，破三郡烏桓于柳城也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Mount Wu Is High》 to 《Slaughter at Willow City》, referring to Lord Cao crossing the northern passes, crossing White Sandalwood, and destroying the three-commandery Wuhuan at Willow City.
translations.idiomatic: 《Mount Wu Is High》 was retitled 《Slaughter at Willow City》, describing Cao Cao's thrust beyond the northern frontier, march through Baitan, and crushing of the three Wuhuan commanderies at Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 改《上陵》為《平南荊》，言曹公平荊州也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Ascending the Mausoleum》 to 《Pacifying Southern Jing》, referring to Lord Cao's pacification of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: 《Ascending the Mausoleum》 became 《Pacifying Southern Jing》, for Cao Cao's conquest of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 改《將進酒》為《平關中》，言曹公征馬超，定關中也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Wine, Advance!》 to 《Pacifying Guanzhong》, referring to Lord Cao's expedition against Ma Chao and settling Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: 《Wine, Advance!》 turned into 《Pacifying Guanzhong》, marking Cao Cao's campaign against Ma Chao and the stabilization of the Guanzhong plain.

sentences.zh: 改《有所思》為《應帝期》，言文帝以聖德受命，應運期也。

translations.literal: They changed 《I Had Someone in Mind》 to 《Answering Heaven's Timetable》, referring to how Emperor Wen, with sagely virtue, received the mandate and answered the timely cycle.
translations.idiomatic: 《I Had Someone in Mind》 was renamed 《Meeting Heaven's Deadlines》, because Emperor Wen's sacred virtue answered the scheduled mandate.

sentences.zh: 改《芳樹》為《邕熙》，言魏氏臨其國，君臣邕穆，庶績咸熙也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Fragrant Trees》 to 《Harmonious Splendor》, referring to how the Wei court ruled its realm, ruler and ministers harmoniously solemn, and every task blazed with order.
translations.idiomatic: 《Fragrant Trees》 became 《Concord and Glory》, depicting Wei rule at home: sovereign and ministers in dignified accord and every office radiant with achievement.

sentences.zh: 改《上邪》為《太和》，言明帝繼體承統，太和改元，德澤流布也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Oh Heaven Above》 to 《Grand Harmony》, referring to how Emperor Ming succeeded to the unified body politic, adopted the Grand Harmony era-name, and kindly dew spread abroad.
translations.idiomatic: 《Oh Heaven Above》 was changed to 《Grand Harmony》, since Emperor Ming inherited the undivided succession, inaugurated the Taihe reign, and virtue moistened the realm.

sentences.zh: 其餘並同舊名。

translations.literal: The remainder kept their old names.
translations.idiomatic: The other titles stayed as before.

sentences.zh: 是時吳亦使韋昭制十二曲名，以述功德受命。

translations.literal: At that time Wu likewise commissioned Wei Zhao to fashion twelve tune titles to recount merit and virtue and receiving the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Wu at the same time ordered Wei Zhao to draft twelve new titles praising its merit and heaven's charge.

sentences.zh: 改《硃鷺》為《炎精缺》，言漢室衰，孫堅奮迅猛志，念在匡救，王跡始乎此也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Red Egret》 to 《The Fire Essence Wanes》, referring to Han's decline and how Sun Jian roused fierce resolve intent on rescue, royal traces beginning here.
translations.idiomatic: 《Red Egret》 became 《The Han Flame Falters》, telling how Sun Jian roused himself when the dynasty weakened and royal enterprise began there.

sentences.zh: 改《思悲翁》為《漢之季》，言堅悼漢之微，痛董卓之亂，興兵奮擊，功蓋海內也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Thinking of the Old Man》 to 《Han in Its Closing Years》, referring to Jian's mourning Han's decline and loathing Dong Zhuo's rebellion, raising troops in fierce strike, merit covering the realm within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: 《Thinking of the Old Man》 became 《Han in Twilight》, mourning the ruined house, denouncing Dong Zhuo's rising storm, and celebrating Sun Jian's armies that shook the realm.

sentences.zh: 改《艾如張》為《攄武師》，言權卒父之業而征伐也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Spreading Mugwort Like a Net》 to 《Unsheathing the Host》, referring to Sun Quan carrying on his father's enterprise and campaigning.
translations.idiomatic: 《Spreading Mugwort》 became 《Mobilizing the Army》, for Sun Quan's continuation of his father's wars.

sentences.zh: 改《上之回》為《烏林》，言魏武既破荊州，順流東下，欲來爭鋒，權命將周瑜逆擊之于烏林而破走也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Ascending to the Turn》 to 《Wulin》, referring to how after Wei Wu broke Jingzhou he flowed east seeking battle, and Sun Quan ordered Zhou Yu to strike him at Wulin and rout him.
translations.idiomatic: 《Ascending to the Turn》 became 《Wulin》, when Cao Cao swept downriver after taking Jingzhou and Zhou Yu met him at Wulin and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 改《雍離》為《秋風》，言權悅以使人，人忘其死也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Yong Leaves Part》 to 《Autumn Wind》, referring to how Sun Quan delighted in employing men so that men forgot death.
translations.idiomatic: 《Yong Leaves Part》 was titled 《Autumn Wind》, praising Sun Quan's delight in worthy officers who forgot their own lives.

sentences.zh: 改《戰城南》為《克皖城》，言魏武志圖並兼，而權親征，破之於皖也。

translations.literal: They changed 《South of the City We Fight》 to 《Taking Wancheng》, referring to how Wei Wu plotted annexation but Sun Quan campaigned in person and defeated him at Wan.
translations.idiomatic: 《South of the City We Fight》 became 《Capture of Wancheng》, when Cao Cao dreamed of swallowing Wu yet Sun Quan led his hosts and shattered him at Wan.

sentences.zh: 改《巫山高》為《關背德》，言蜀將關羽背棄吳德，權引師浮江而擒之也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Mount Wu Is High》 to 《Guan Betrays Virtue》, referring to Shu general Guan Yu betraying Wu's good faith, Sun Quan leading his army on the river and capturing him.
translations.idiomatic: 《Mount Wu Is High》 became 《Guan Forsakes Good Faith》, narrating Guan Yu's breach with Wu and Sun Quan's river offensive that seized him.

sentences.zh: 改《上陵曲》為通荊州，言權與蜀交好齊盟，中有關羽自失之愆，終復初好也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Ascending the Mausoleum Tune》 to 《Opening Communications with Jingzhou》, referring to how Sun Quan and Shu allied in good faith, yet Guan Yu's own fault came between them, and in the end early friendship was restored.
translations.idiomatic: 《Ascending the Mausoleum》 became 《Reopening Jingzhou》, for the Shu-Wu alliance troubled by Guan Yu's error and later healed.

sentences.zh: 改《將進酒》為《章洪德》，言權章其大德，而遠方來附也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Wine, Advance!》 to 《Manifesting Vast Virtue》, referring to how Sun Quan displayed his great virtue and the distant came to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: 《Wine, Advance!》 became 《Proclaiming Mighty Virtue》, when distant peoples rallied to Sun Quan's evident power.

sentences.zh: 改《有所思》為《順歷數》，言權順籙圖之符，而建大號也。

translations.literal: They changed 《I Had Someone in Mind》 to 《Following the Tallies' Sequence》, referring to how Sun Quan followed the tallies and charts and assumed the grand title.
translations.idiomatic: 《I Had Someone in Mind》 turned into 《Obeying the Tally's Order》, marking Sun Quan's accession in accord with portents.

sentences.zh: 改《芳樹》為《承天命》，言其時主聖德踐位，道化至盛也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Fragrant Trees》 to 《Receiving Heaven's Mandate》, referring to how at that time the ruler's sacred virtue mounted the throne and transforming influence reached utmost flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: 《Fragrant Trees》 became 《Accepting Heaven's Charge》, celebrating the ruler enthroned and transformation at its height.

sentences.zh: 改《上邪曲》為《玄化》，言其時主修文武，則天而行，仁澤流洽，天下喜樂也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Oh Heaven Above Tune》 to 《Dark Transforming Influence》, referring to how at that time the ruler cultivated civil and martial arts, modeled himself on Heaven, kindly moisture spread everywhere, and all under heaven rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: 《Oh Heaven Above》 was renamed 《Profound Transformation》, praising civil-martial cultivation that mirrored heaven and brought joy to all.

sentences.zh: 其餘亦用舊名不改。

translations.literal: The rest likewise kept old names unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining titles again stayed as they were.

sentences.zh: 及武帝受禪，乃令傅玄制為二十二篇，亦述以功德代魏。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted abdication, he ordered Fu Xuan to compose twenty-two pieces, likewise narrating merit and virtue replacing Wei.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu took the abdicated throne he told Fu Xuan to write twenty-two lyrics chronicling Jin merit supplanting Wei.

sentences.zh: 改《硃鷺》為《靈之祥》，言宣帝之佐魏，猶虞舜之事堯，既有石瑞之徵，又能用武以誅孟達之逆命也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Red Egret》 to 《Auspice of the Numina》, referring to how Emperor Xuan aided Wei as Yu Shun served Yao, having both the omen of stone talisman and the ability to use arms to execute Meng Da's treasonous command.
translations.idiomatic: 《Red Egret》 became 《Omen of the Spirits》, likening Sima Yi's service to Wei to Shun serving Yao: stone omens appeared and arms crushed Meng Da's revolt.

sentences.zh: 改《思悲翁》為《宣受命》，言宣帝御諸葛亮，養威重，運神兵，亮震怖而死也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Thinking of the Old Man》 to 《Xuan Receives the Mandate》, referring to how Emperor Xuan opposed Zhuge Liang, nurtured awe-inspiring weight, deployed spirit-like troops, and Liang trembled with terror and died.
translations.idiomatic: 《Thinking of the Old Man》 became 《Xuan Takes the Charge》, describing Sima Yi's stalemate with Zhuge Liang—stored dread majesty, maneuvered subtle hosts—until Zhuge Liang died of shock.

sentences.zh: 改《艾如張》為《征遼東》，言宣帝陵大海之表，討滅公孫氏而梟其首也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Spreading Mugwort》 to 《Campaigning Liaodong》, referring to how Emperor Xuan crossed beyond the great sea, attacked and destroyed the Gongsun clan, and exposed their leader's head.
translations.idiomatic: 《Spreading Mugwort》 was titled 《The Liaodong Expedition》, for Sima Yi's crossing of the sea, destruction of the Gongsuns, and display of Gongsun Yuan's head.

sentences.zh: 改《上之回》為《宣輔政》，言宣帝聖道深遠，撥亂反正，網羅文武之才，以定二儀之序也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Ascending to the Turn》 to 《Xuan Assists the Government》, referring to how Emperor Xuan's sagely way ran deep, set chaos aright and restored order, netted civil and martial talents, and fixed the pattern of the Two Powers.
translations.idiomatic: 《Ascending to the Turn》 became 《Xuan Orders the Realm》, praising deep sagely policy that righted disorder and ranked talented civil and martial officers.

sentences.zh: 改《雍離》為《時運多難》，言宣帝致討吳方，有征無戰也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Yong Leaves Part》 to 《The Age Harrows with Many Hardships》, referring to how Emperor Xuan carried punitive expedition to Wu's territory—campaigns without battle.
translations.idiomatic: 《Yong Leaves Part》 turned into 《Times of Many Perils》, noting punitive moves toward Wu that ended without pitched battle.

sentences.zh: 改《戰城南》為《景龍飛》，言景帝克明威教，賞順夷逆，隆無疆，崇洪基也。

translations.literal: They changed 《South of the City We Fight》 to 《Scenic Dragon Soars》, referring to how Emperor Jing clarified awesome instruction, rewarded compliance and chastised rebellion, elevated boundlessness, and enlarged the mighty foundation.
translations.idiomatic: 《South of the City We Fight》 became 《Soaring Dragon of Splendor》, celebrating Emperor Jing's awe-education, rewarding the loyal, punishing rebels, widening blessing, and deepening the great base.

sentences.zh: 改《巫山高》為《平玉衡》，言景帝一萬國之殊風，齊四海之乖心，禮賢養士，而纂洪業也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Mount Wu Is High》 to 《Leveling the Jade Balance》, referring to how Emperor Jing unified the myriad nations' diverse customs, aligned the four seas' contrary hearts, honored the worthy and nurtured knights, and continued the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: 《Mount Wu Is High》 was renamed 《Trueing the Jade Armillary》, for Emperor Jing's harmonizing every region, aligning distant hearts, honoring worthies, and advancing the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 改《上陵》為《文皇統百揆》，言文帝始統百揆，用人有序，以敷太平之化也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Ascending the Mausoleum》 to 《Emperor Wen Commands All Offices》, referring to how Emperor Wen first presided over all bureaus, employed men in due order, and spread the transforming influence of great peace.
translations.idiomatic: 《Ascending the Mausoleum》 became 《Emperor Wen Governs All Bureaus》, because Sima Zhao first superintended every office, ordered appointments, and spread great peace.

sentences.zh: 改《將進酒》為《因時運》，言因時運變，聖謀潛施，解長蛇之交，離群桀之党，以武濟文，以邁其德也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Wine, Advance!》 to 《Riding the Season's Fortune》, referring to how following fortune's seasons the sacred stratagem worked in secret, undid the long-serpent alliance, split the pack of fiends, aided culture with arms, and thereby advanced virtue.
translations.idiomatic: 《Wine, Advance!》 was titled 《Seizing the Hour》, describing timely stratagem that broke Shu-Wu collusion, shattered rebel cliques, paired arms with culture, and heightened virtue.

sentences.zh: 改《有所思》為《惟庸蜀》，言文帝既平萬乘之蜀，封建萬國，復五等之爵也。

translations.literal: They changed 《I Had Someone in Mind》 to 《Only That Shu》, referring to how Emperor Wen pacified the Shu host of ten thousand chariots, enfeoffed myriad states, and restored the five grades of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: 《I Had Someone in Mind》 became 《That Shu Alone》, for Sima Zhao's reduction of the Shu empire, investiture of countless domains, and revival of the five noble ranks.

sentences.zh: 改《芳樹》為《天序》，言聖皇應曆受禪，弘濟大化，用人各盡其才也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Fragrant Trees》 to 《Heaven's Ordering》, referring to how the sage emperor answered the calendar and received abdication, broadly aided great transformation, and employed each man to his full talent.
translations.idiomatic: 《Fragrant Trees》 turned into 《Heaven's Sequence》, celebrating the sage ruler's calendar-abdication, vast transformation, and each talent fully used.

sentences.zh: 改《上邪》為《大晉承運期》，言聖皇應籙受圖，化象神明也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Oh Heaven Above》 to 《Great Jin Receives the Mandate's Season》, referring to how the sage emperor answered the tallies and received the charts, transforming likeness spirit-like.
translations.idiomatic: 《Oh Heaven Above》 became 《Great Jin's Hour》, because the sage sovereign answered the tally-charts and merged his likeness with the divine.

sentences.zh: 改《君馬黃》為《金靈運》，言聖皇踐阼，致敬宗廟，而孝道行於天下也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Your Horse Is Yellow》 to 《The Metal Essence's Course》, referring to how the sage emperor ascended the throne, paid utmost homage at the ancestral shrine, and filial devotion ran through the realm.
translations.idiomatic: 《Your Horse Is Yellow》 was renamed 《Metal Virtue in Motion》, praising accession, ancestral devotion, and filial teaching across the land.

sentences.zh: 改《雉子班》為《于穆我皇》，言聖皇受禪，德合神明也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Pheasant Broods》 to 《Oh Solemn Our Sovereign》, referring to how the sage emperor received abdication and virtue matched spirit luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: 《Pheasant Broods》 became 《How Majestic Our King》, for the abdicated accession and virtue mirroring the gods.

sentences.zh: 改《聖人出》為《仲春振旅》，言大晉申文武之教，畋獵以時也。

translations.literal: They changed 《The Sage Appears》 to 《Second Month Drills the Host》, referring to how Great Jin extended civil and martial teaching and hunted according to season.
translations.idiomatic: 《The Sage Appears》 was titled 《Spring Hunt Drills the Troops》, recording Jin extension of civil-martial instruction and seasonal hunts.

sentences.zh: 改《臨高臺》為《夏苗田》，言大晉畋狩順時，為苗除害也。

translations.literal: They changed 《From the High Terrace》 to 《Summer Seedling Hunt》, referring to how Great Jin hunted in accord with season to rid the fields of harm.
translations.idiomatic: 《From the High Terrace》 became 《Summer Seedling Hunt》, when Jin drove off vermin in accord with the calendar.

sentences.zh: 改《遠如期》為《仲秋獮田》，言大晉雖有文德，不廢武事，順時以殺伐也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Far as the Promised Day》 to 《Second Month Autumn Hunt》, referring to how Great Jin, though possessing civil virtue, did not neglect martial affairs, following season for punitive strikes.
translations.idiomatic: 《Far as the Promised Day》 turned into 《Autumn Hunt in Order》, insisting that even with civil splendor Jin still struck punishments on schedule.

sentences.zh: 改《石留》為《順天道》，言仲冬大閱，用武修文，大晉之德配天也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Stone Stays》 to 《Obeying Heaven's Way》, referring to how in mid-winter the grand review used arms to cultivate culture, Great Jin's virtue matching heaven.
translations.idiomatic: 《Stone Stays》 was renamed 《Following Heaven's Road》, for midwinter grand reviews where arms perfected culture and Jin matched heaven.

sentences.zh: 改《務成》為《唐堯》，言聖皇陟帝位，德化光四表也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Accomplishing Completion》 to 《Tang Yao》, referring to how the sage emperor ascended the throne of emperor and moral transformation irradiated the four outer regions.
translations.idiomatic: 《Accomplishing Completion》 became 《Emperor Yao of Tang》, because the sage ruler mounted the throne and edifying virtue lit the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 《玄雲》依舊名，言聖皇用人，各盡其材也。

translations.literal: 《Dark Clouds》 kept its old name, referring to how the sage emperor employed men, each to his material.
translations.idiomatic: 《Dark Clouds》 stayed unchanged, depicting every talent placed according to his gifts.

sentences.zh: 改《黃爵行》為《伯益》，言赤烏銜書，有周以興，今聖皇受命，神雀來也。

translations.literal: They changed 《Yellow Sparrow March》 to 《Boy Yi》, referring to how the red crow bore writing—Zhou rose thereby—and now the sage emperor received the mandate and spirit magpies came.
translations.idiomatic: 《Yellow Sparrow March》 became 《Helper Yi》, comparing the crimson crow's writ that launched Zhou to the spirit finches greeting Jin's charge.

sentences.zh: 《釣竿》依舊名，言聖皇德配堯舜，又有呂望之佐，濟大功，致太平也。

translations.literal: 《Fishing Rod》 kept its old name, referring to how the sage emperor's virtue matched Yao and Shun and he also had Lü Wang's assistance to accomplish great work and bring about great peace.
translations.idiomatic: 《Fishing Rod》 remained, pairing Jin virtue with Yao-Shun and Lü Wang's aid to finish the great task of peace.

sentences.zh: 其辭並列之於後雲。

translations.literal: Their lyrics are all listed below.
translations.idiomatic: The texts follow in order.

sentences.zh: 靈之祥

translations.literal: Auspice of the Numina
translations.idiomatic: Auspice of the Numina

sentences.zh: 靈之祥，石瑞章。

translations.literal: Auspice of the numina—stone omens bright.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit blessing—stone portents blaze.

sentences.zh: 旌金德，出西方。

translations.literal: Displaying metal virtue, emerging from the west.
translations.idiomatic: Metal virtue revealed, rising from the west.

sentences.zh: 天降命，授宣皇。

translations.literal: Heaven dropped the charge, bestowed on Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sent its mandate, granting Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 應期運，時龍驤。

translations.literal: Answering timely fortune, for the moment the dragon rears.
translations.idiomatic: He rides the hour's luck; the dragon rears on high.

sentences.zh: 繼大舜，佐陶唐。

translations.literal: Continuing great Shun, assisting lofty Tang.
translations.idiomatic: He follows Great Shun, assists lofty Tang.

sentences.zh: 贊武文，建帝綱。

translations.literal: Praising civil and martial, establishing imperial norm.
translations.idiomatic: He upholds civil and martial, sets the royal span.

sentences.zh: 孟氏叛，據南疆。

translations.literal: The Meng clan rebelled, holding the southern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Da rebelled, gripping the southern marches.

sentences.zh: 追有扈，亂五常。

translations.literal: Pursuing the You-Hu, disordering the five constants.
translations.idiomatic: Like punishing You-Hu, he smashes the five norms.

sentences.zh: 吳寇叛，蜀虜強。

translations.literal: Wu bandits rebelled; Shu captives strong.
translations.idiomatic: Wu raiders rise; Shu hosts stay fierce.

sentences.zh: 交誓盟，連遐荒。

translations.literal: Swearing leagues of alliance, linking distant wastes.
translations.idiomatic: They swear dire alliances, chain the far frontiers.

sentences.zh: 宣赫怒，奮鷹揚。

translations.literal: Xuan roused fierce wrath, soaring like the hawk.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan vents fierce wrath, lifts wings like hawks.

sentences.zh: 震乾威，曜電光。

translations.literal: Shaking heaven's majesty, flashing lightning's gleam.
translations.idiomatic: He shakes celestial awe, flashes lightning sheen.

sentences.zh: 陵九天，陷石城。

translations.literal: Scaling the nine heavens, toppling Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: He climbs the nine tiers, storms Stone Fort hold.

sentences.zh: 梟逆命，拯有生。

translations.literal: Beheading the traitor's mandate, saving the living throng.
translations.idiomatic: He cuts the rebel charge, saves the breathing folk.

sentences.zh: 萬國安，四海寧。

translations.literal: Ten thousand lands secure; the four seas at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand regions rest; four seas grow calm.

sentences.zh: 宣受命

translations.literal: Xuan Receives the Mandate
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Receives the Mandate

sentences.zh: 宣受命，應天機，風雲時動神龍飛。

translations.literal: Xuan receives the mandate, answers heaven's instrument; wind and clouds move in season—divine dragon flies.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan takes heaven's charge; clouds ride the hour—the dragon lifts.

sentences.zh: 禦葛亮，鎮雍梁。

translations.literal: He fences off Zhuge Liang, guards Yong and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He bars Zhuge Liang, shields Yong and Liang.

sentences.zh: 邊境安，夷夏康。

translations.literal: Borderlands secure; barbarians and Xia at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Frontiers lock tight; tribes and heartland easy.

sentences.zh: 務節事，勤定傾。

translations.literal: He attends to modest duty, toils to steady the tipping scale.
translations.idiomatic: He trims state affairs, labors to right the leaning throne.

sentences.zh: 攬英雄，保持盈。

translations.literal: He gathers heroes, holds fullness in care.
translations.idiomatic: He collects champions, guards surplus with care.

sentences.zh: 深穆穆，赫明明。

translations.literal: Profound and solemn, radiant and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Deep and still, blazingly bright.

sentences.zh: 沖而泰，天之經。

translations.literal: Subtle and tranquil—heaven's constant warp.
translations.idiomatic: Supple and still—the warp of heaven.

sentences.zh: 養威重，運神兵。

translations.literal: He nurtures dread majesty, wields spirit-like troops.
translations.idiomatic: He stores dread weight, drives spirit-like hosts.

sentences.zh: 亮乃震斃，天下安寧。

translations.literal: Liang then quaked and perished; all under heaven secure and still.
translations.idiomatic: Liang dies of dread; the realm lies quiet.

sentences.zh: 征遼東

translations.literal: Campaigning Liaodong
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning Liaodong

sentences.zh: 征遼東，敵失據，威靈邁日域。

translations.literal: Campaigning Liaodong—foe loses foothold; dread majesty crosses the sun's realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Liaodong war—foes lose footing; awe crosses the solar sphere.

sentences.zh: 公孫既授首，群逆破膽，咸震怖。

translations.literal: Gongsun beheaded; crowd of rebels' gall melts—all shake in terror.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Yuan loses his head; rebels melt with fear.

sentences.zh: 朔北回應，海表景附。

translations.literal: The northern north responds; beyond the seas gaze and cling like shadows.
translations.idiomatic: The northern wastes answer; overseas shores cling like shadows.

sentences.zh: 武功赫赫，德雲布。

translations.literal: Martial prowess shines terrifying; virtue spreads like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: His martial glory blazes; kindness rains like clouds.

sentences.zh: 宣輔政

translations.literal: Xuan Assists the Government
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Assists the Government

sentences.zh: 宣皇輔政，聖烈深。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan aids governance; sagely merit runs deep.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuan emperor steered the realm; sacred power ran profound.

sentences.zh: 撥亂反正，順天心。

translations.literal: He sets chaos aright and restores orthodoxy; he accords with heaven's heart.
translations.idiomatic: He straightened the turmoil and matched heaven's mind.

sentences.zh: 網羅文武才，慎厥所生。

translations.literal: He nets civil and martial talents; cautiously he nurtures what they bear.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered civil and martial talent and fostered each calling.

sentences.zh: 所生賢，遺教施。

translations.literal: What they bear proves worthy; his bequeathed teaching spreads.
translations.idiomatic: Those nurtured proved worthy; his legacy spread as doctrine.

sentences.zh: 安上治民，化風移。

translations.literal: He settles superiors and governs the people; transforming customs shift.
translations.idiomatic: He steadied ruler and folk and shifted customs through reform.

sentences.zh: 肇創帝基，洪業垂。

translations.literal: He begins creation of the imperial foundation; vast enterprise hangs down.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the dynastic base and hung the great enterprise forth.

sentences.zh: 于鑠明明，時赫戲。

translations.literal: Oh, blaze so bright, splendid and shining, momentous display.
translations.idiomatic: How radiant his gleam, how fierce his shining play.

sentences.zh: 功濟萬世，定二儀。

translations.literal: Merit aids ten thousand generations; he fixes the Two Powers.
translations.idiomatic: His work aids endless ages; he set heaven and earth aright.

sentences.zh: 定二儀，雲行雨施，海外風馳。

translations.literal: Fixing the Two Powers: clouds move and rain falls; beyond the seas winds gallop.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth aligned: clouds rode, rain fell, winds raced overseas.

sentences.zh: 時運多難

translations.literal: The Age Harrows with Many Hardships
translations.idiomatic: The Age Harrows with Many Hardships

sentences.zh: 時運多難，道教痡。

translations.literal: The age harrows with many hardships; the Way's teaching grows weary.
translations.idiomatic: Hard times exhausted the Way; instruction grew thin.

sentences.zh: 天地變化，有盈虛。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth alter and shift; there is fullness and emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: Sky and soil alternate between wax and wane.

sentences.zh: 蠢爾吳蠻，武視江湖。

translations.literal: You foolish Wu barbarians--martially you gaze on rivers and lakes.
translations.idiomatic: Those Wu savages eyed the rivers with martial greed.

sentences.zh: 我皇赫斯，致天誅。

translations.literal: Our emperor awesome thus--brings heaven's punishment upon you.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign rose in wrath to wield heaven's scourge.

sentences.zh: 有征無戰，弭其圖。

translations.literal: Where there is campaign there is no battle; your plots are stilled.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns ended without pitched battle; their schemes collapsed.

sentences.zh: 天威橫被，廓東隅。

translations.literal: Heaven's majesty spreads horizontally; opens the eastern corner.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's awe swept outward and cleared the eastern march.

sentences.zh: 景龍飛

translations.literal: Scenic Dragon Soars
translations.idiomatic: Scenic Dragon Soars

sentences.zh: 景龍飛，禦天威。

translations.literal: Scenic dragon soars--he wields heaven's majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The dazzling dragon mounts heaven's dread majesty.

sentences.zh: 聰鑒玄察，動與神明協機。

translations.literal: Keen mirror darkly probes; movement joins spirit luminaries' pivot.
translations.idiomatic: His subtle insight pierced all; motion matched the gods' hinge.

sentences.zh: 從之者顯，逆之者滅夷。

translations.literal: Those who follow shine bright; those who oppose are wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Followers flourished; opponents were extinguished.

sentences.zh: 文教敷，武功巍。

translations.literal: Civil patterns spread; martial merit towers.
translations.idiomatic: Culture spread wide; arms stood tall.

sentences.zh: 普被四海，萬邦望風，莫不來綏。

translations.literal: Universally covering the four seas--ten thousand lands gaze on the wind; none fail to come and submit.
translations.idiomatic: His cloak covered the seas; every realm watched and sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 聖德潛斷，先天弗違。

translations.literal: Sagely virtue secretly decides; before heaven he does not rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Sacred virtue judged unseen; he never fought heaven's intent.

sentences.zh: 弗違祥，享世永長。

translations.literal: Not rebelling auspicious signs; enjoying the age forever long.
translations.idiomatic: No ill omens lingered; his reign stretched long.

sentences.zh: 猛以致寬，道化光。

translations.literal: Fierce to bring breadth; transforming influence shines.
translations.idiomatic: Severity opened into breadth; his transformation gleamed.

sentences.zh: 赫明明，祚隆無疆。

translations.literal: Brilliantly bright--blessing lofty without bound.
translations.idiomatic: Radiance supreme; blessing without frontier.

sentences.zh: 帝績惟期，有命既集，崇此洪基。

translations.literal: Imperial merit awaits its season--the charge already gathered--exalts this mighty foundation.
translations.idiomatic: His deed awaited heaven's hour; the mandate gathered to lift this throne.

sentences.zh: 平玉衡

translations.literal: Leveling the Jade Balance
translations.idiomatic: Leveling the Jade Balance

sentences.zh: 平玉衡，糾奸回。

translations.literal: Leveling the jade balance--correcting treacherous deviation.
translations.idiomatic: He trueed the cosmic scales and straightened treason's bend.

sentences.zh: 萬國殊風，四海乖。

translations.literal: Ten thousand lands, diverse customs; four seas at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Every realm bore other manners; the seas pulled apart.

sentences.zh: 禮賢養士，羈禦英雄，思心齊。

translations.literal: Honoring worthies and nurturing knights--bridling and ruling heroes--thoughts and hearts aligned.
translations.idiomatic: He honored men of worth, fed champions of war, haltered heroes until minds met.

sentences.zh: 纂戎洪業，崇皇階。

translations.literal: Continuing martial enterprise--exalting the imperial stairs.
translations.idiomatic: He carried on arms and magnified the throne.

sentences.zh: 品物咸亨，聖敬日躋。

translations.literal: All manner of things flourish together; sagely reverence mounts daily.
translations.idiomatic: Creation prospered together; sacred awe climbed each day.

sentences.zh: 聰鑒盡下情，明明綜天機。

translations.literal: Keen mirror exhausts conditions below; brilliantly bright he threads heaven's pivot.
translations.idiomatic: His mirror drained every grievance below; bright clarity ran heaven's loom.

sentences.zh: 文皇統百揆

translations.literal: Emperor Wen Commands All Offices
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen Commands All Offices

sentences.zh: 文皇統百揆，繼天理萬方。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen commands all offices--continuing heaven's pattern over myriad directions.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen ruled every bureau and extended heaven's pattern to all lands.

sentences.zh: 武將鎮四隅，英佐盈朝堂，謀言協秋蘭，清風發其芳。

translations.literal: Martial generals guard the four corners; splendid aides fill the morning hall--counsel harmonizes like autumn orchids; pure breeze sends forth their fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: Generals held the four marches; wise men packed the hall; counsel chimed like autumn orchids on a clear wind.

sentences.zh: 洪澤所漸潤，礫石為珪璋。

translations.literal: Where flood virtue gradually soaks--gravel stones become jade scepters.
translations.idiomatic: His soaking virtue turned grit into ritual jade.

sentences.zh: 大道侔五帝，盛德逾三王。

translations.literal: Great Way equals the Five Emperors--surpassing virtue exceeds the Three Kings.
translations.idiomatic: His Dao matched the Five Thearchs; kindness overtopped the Three Kings.

sentences.zh: 咸光大，上參天與地，至化無內外。

translations.literal: Together they enlarge brilliance--above joining heaven and earth--ultimate transformation knows no inner or outer.
translations.idiomatic: Their glory joined sky and soil; transformation knew no inside or out.

sentences.zh: 無內外，六合並康乂。

translations.literal: No inner or outer--six directions together calm and ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Without inner or outer strife, the six reaches stood ordered.

sentences.zh: 並康乂，遘茲嘉會。

translations.literal: Together calm and ordered--meeting now this auspicious assembly.
translations.idiomatic: All corners healed together in this blessed hour.

sentences.zh: 在昔羲與農，大晉德斯邁。

translations.literal: In antiquity Xi and Nong--Great Jin's virtue strides beyond.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and Nong of old watched Great Jin stride past them.

sentences.zh: 鎮征及諸州，為籓衛。

translations.literal: Town garrisons and the provinces--serve as fence and shield.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisons and provinces became fence and shield.

sentences.zh: 功濟四海，洪烈流萬世。

translations.literal: Merit aids the four seas--vast merit flows ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: His benefit soaked the seas; mighty deeds echo forever.

sentences.zh: 因時運

translations.literal: Riding the Season's Fortune
translations.idiomatic: Riding the Season's Fortune

sentences.zh: 因時運，聖策施。

translations.literal: Riding the season's fortune--sacred stratagem deploys.
translations.idiomatic: He rode the hour's luck and set sacred plans in motion.

sentences.zh: 長蛇交解，群桀離。

translations.literal: Long-serpent alliance undone--pack of fiends scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The serpent alliance split; rebel cliques fled.

sentences.zh: 勢窮奔吳，獸騎厲。

translations.literal: Strength spent, fleeing to Wu--mounted beasts ride fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Broken, they raced to Wu on beasts that flew.

sentences.zh: 惟武進，審大計。

translations.literal: Only martial advance--deliberating grand plans.
translations.idiomatic: Force marched while counsel weighed the grand design.

sentences.zh: 時邁其德，清一世。

translations.literal: The season strides his virtue--purifying a whole age.
translations.idiomatic: The age stepped with his virtue and cleansed an era.

sentences.zh: 惟庸蜀

translations.literal: Only That Shu
translations.idiomatic: Only That Shu

sentences.zh: 惟庸蜀，僭號天一隅。

translations.literal: Only that Shu--presumptuously claiming the title, corner of heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Shu alone dared style itself emperor in a forgotten corner.

sentences.zh: 劉備逆帝命，禪亮承其餘。

translations.literal: Liu Bei rebels against the imperial charge--Liu Shan and Zhuge Liang inherit his leavings.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei defied heaven's charge; Liu Shan and Zhuge Liang drew out his unfinished war.

sentences.zh: 擁眾數十萬，窺隙乘我虛。

translations.literal: Hugging crowds hundreds of thousands--watching gaps, exploiting our emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: They hugged hosts in hundreds of thousands, seeking cracks in our guard.

sentences.zh: 驛騎進羽檄，天下不遑居。

translations.literal: Courier horses advance feathered summons--the realm had no leisure to dwell.
translations.idiomatic: Express riders bore urgent orders; the empire never rested.

sentences.zh: 姜維屢寇邊，隴上為荒蕪。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei repeatedly raided the borders--Longshang became wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei harried the frontier until Long left fallow.

sentences.zh: 文皇湣斯民，曆世受罪辜。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen pitied these people--through generations suffering guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen mourned the folk long punished by Shu.

sentences.zh: 外謨籓屏臣，內謨眾士夫。

translations.literal: Without--counsel fence-screen ministers; within--counsel hosts of scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: Outside he relied on frontier ministers; inside on every counselor.

sentences.zh: 爪牙應指受，腹心獻良圖。

translations.literal: Talons and fangs answered nod and signal--belly and heart offered fine plans.
translations.idiomatic: His warriors leapt at a glance; his counselors laid perfect plots.

sentences.zh: 良圖協成文，大興百萬軍。

translations.literal: Fine plans harmonized into patterned text--great hosts a million strong arose.
translations.idiomatic: Plans knit into strategy; a million spears rose.

sentences.zh: 雷鼓震地起，猛勢陵浮雲。

translations.literal: Thunder drums shook earth upright--fierce surge overtopped floating clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder drums shook the soil; fury topped the clouds.

sentences.zh: 逋虜畏天誅，面縛造壘門。

translations.literal: Fleeing captives feared heaven's punishment--bound themselves and came to the camp gate.
translations.idiomatic: The beaten feared heaven's blade and came bound to the palisade.

sentences.zh: 萬里同風教，逆命稱妾臣。

translations.literal: Ten thousand miles share wind and teaching--those who rebelled against the charge called themselves concubine-subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Wind and law crossed ten thousand leagues; rebels styled themselves vassals.

sentences.zh: 光建五等，紀綱天人。

translations.literal: Brightly establishing five ranks--nets heaven and man.
translations.idiomatic: He set the five noble ranks and joined heaven with men.

sentences.zh: 天序，應曆受禪，承靈祜。

translations.literal: Heaven's ordering--answering calendar receiving abdication--inheriting spirit blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's sequence met calendar and abdication and drew spirit blessing down.

sentences.zh: 禦群龍，勒螭武。

translations.literal: Driving the flock of dragons--bridling hornless-dragon hosts.
translations.idiomatic: He drove the dragon hosts and reined the hornless armies.

sentences.zh: 弘濟大化，英雋作輔。

translations.literal: Broadly aiding great transformation--heroes serve as aides.
translations.idiomatic: Great transformation spread wide; heroes served as rails.

sentences.zh: 明明統萬機，赫赫鎮四方，咎繇稷契之疇，協蘭芳。

translations.literal: Brilliantly bright commanding myriad pivots--awesomely guarding four quarters--men like Gao Yao, Ji and Qi--orchid fragrance harmonizes.
translations.idiomatic: Bright he ruled ten thousand hinges and guarded four fronts with ministers like Gao Yao, Ji, and Qi, orchid-sweet accord.

sentences.zh: 禮王臣，覆兆民。

translations.literal: Honoring royal ministers--covering hundred-clan people.
translations.idiomatic: He crowned his kingsmen and sheltered every clan.

sentences.zh: 化之如天與地，誰敢愛其身？

translations.literal: Transforming them like heaven and earth--who dares cling to private selves?
translations.idiomatic: He shaped them like heaven and earth; who could withhold loyalty?

sentences.zh: 大晉承運期

translations.literal: Great Jin Receives the Mandate's Season
translations.idiomatic: Great Jin Receives the Mandate's Season

sentences.zh: 大晉承運期，德隆聖皇。

translations.literal: Great Jin receives the mandate's season--virtue lofty, sage emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Great Jin took heaven's hour; virtue rose with the sage throne.

sentences.zh: 時清晏，白日垂光。

translations.literal: Times pure and tranquil--bright sun hangs radiance.
translations.idiomatic: The age grew clear and still; the bright sun hung steady.

sentences.zh: 應籙圖，陟帝位，繼天正玉衡。

translations.literal: Answering tally charts--ascending emperor's throne--continuing heaven, correcting jade armillary.
translations.idiomatic: Portents answered; he mounted the throne and aligned heaven's armillary.

sentences.zh: 化行象神明，至哉道隆虞與唐。

translations.literal: Transforming conduct images spirit luminaries--ultimate indeed Way lofty as Yu and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Conduct mirrored the gods; his Way rivaled Yu and Tang.

sentences.zh: 元首敷洪化，百僚股肱並忠良。

translations.literal: Head spreads vast transformation--hundred officials as thighs and arms, together loyal and good.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign spread vast change; every minister served as limb and loyal heart.

sentences.zh: 時太康，隆隆赫赫，福祚盈無疆。

translations.literal: Times reach Grand Peace--towering and blazing--blessing throne overflows without bound.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Kang dawned in towering blaze; blessing flooded without limit.

sentences.zh: 金靈運

translations.literal: Metal Essence's Course
translations.idiomatic: Metal Essence's Course

sentences.zh: 金靈運，天符發。

translations.literal: Metal essence moves--heaven's tally issues.
translations.idiomatic: Metal virtue stirred; heaven gave its token.

sentences.zh: 聖徵見，參日月。

translations.literal: Sacred omens appear--joining sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: Sacred signs appeared beside sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 惟我皇，體神聖。

translations.literal: Only our emperor--embodies spirit sagacity.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign bodies forth spirit-wisdom.

sentences.zh: 受魏禪，應天命。

translations.literal: Receiving Wei's abdication--answering heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: He took Wei's abdication and answered heaven.

sentences.zh: 皇之興，靈有徵。

translations.literal: Emperor's rising--spirit has omens.
translations.idiomatic: His ascent bore spirit omens.

sentences.zh: 登大麓，禦萬乘。

translations.literal: Ascending great foothills--ruling myriad chariots.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed the sacred mound and drove myriad cars.

sentences.zh: 皇之輔，若闞武。

translations.literal: Emperor's aides--like Tiger Guards keen.
translations.idiomatic: His aides matched Tiger Guard zeal.

sentences.zh: 爪牙奮，莫之禦。

translations.literal: Talons and nails rouse--none withstand them.
translations.idiomatic: Claws sprang forth; none could block them.

sentences.zh: 皇之佐，贊清化。

translations.literal: Emperor's assistants--assist pure transformation.
translations.idiomatic: His helpers aided pure reform.

sentences.zh: 百事理，萬邦賀。

translations.literal: Hundred affairs ordered--ten thousand lands rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: Every office aligned; myriad realms rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 神祗應，嘉瑞章。

translations.literal: Spirits respond--auspicious omens bright.
translations.idiomatic: Gods answered; bright omens shone.

sentences.zh: 恭享禮，薦先皇。

translations.literal: Reverently enjoying ritual--offering to former emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He worshipped with care and fed the late emperor's spirit.

sentences.zh: 樂時奏，磬管鏘。

translations.literal: Joyfully timed performance--chimes and pipes clang.
translations.idiomatic: Music rose on cue; stones and winds rang.

sentences.zh: 鼓殷殷，鐘鍠鍠。

translations.literal: Drums deep-thunder--bells vast-clang.
translations.idiomatic: Drums thundered deep; bells crashed wide.

sentences.zh: 奠樽俎，實玉觴。

translations.literal: Setting goblet stands--filling jade cups.
translations.idiomatic: He set the trays and poured jade cups full.

sentences.zh: 神歆饗，咸悅康。

translations.literal: Spirits savor and feast--all rejoice in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits feasted; every heart grew calm.

sentences.zh: 宴孫子，祐無疆。

translations.literal: Feasting grandsons--blessing without bound.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted grandsons; blessing knew no bound.

sentences.zh: 大孝蒸蒸，德教被萬方。

translations.literal: Great filial devotion steams upward--virtuous teaching covers myriad directions.
translations.idiomatic: Filial steam rose thick; moral rain soaked every quarter.

sentences.zh: 于穆我皇

translations.literal: Oh Solemn Our Sovereign
translations.idiomatic: Oh Solemn Our Sovereign

sentences.zh: 于穆我皇，盛德聖且明。

translations.literal: Oh solemn our emperor--flourishing virtue, sage and bright.
translations.idiomatic: How solemn our sovereign, sage virtue blazing bright.

sentences.zh: 受禪君世，光濟群生。

translations.literal: Receiving abdication he rules the age; glory aids the throng of lives.
translations.idiomatic: He took abdication to shepherd the age and succor every life.

sentences.zh: 普天率土，莫不來庭。

translations.literal: Throughout heaven's span and earth's soil--none fail to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Under heaven and across the soil every realm presents itself at court.

sentences.zh: 顒顒六合內，望風仰泰清。

translations.literal: Within the six directions all lift eyes--gazing on the wind they honor Grand Peace.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the six reaches every gaze turns upward, awaiting merciful clarity.

sentences.zh: 萬國雍雍，興頌聲。

translations.literal: Ten thousand lands harmonious--rising hymn of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Myriad kingdoms move as one; praise rises everywhere.

sentences.zh: 大化洽，地平而天成。

translations.literal: Great transformation everywhere permeates; earth level and heaven completed.
translations.idiomatic: Great peace soaks every corner; earth lies flat and heaven holds firm.

sentences.zh: 七政齊，玉衡惟平。

translations.literal: Seven regulators aligned; jade armillary alone stands level.
translations.idiomatic: The seven celestial powers line up; the jade squaring-weight stays true.

sentences.zh: 峨峨佐命，濟濟群英。

translations.literal: Lofty the ministers who aid the charge; thronging the host of heroes.
translations.idiomatic: Towering stand the ministers who answered heaven; countless heroes throng.

sentences.zh: 夙夜乾乾，萬機是經。

translations.literal: From dawn to dusk diligent; myriad pivots are threaded.
translations.idiomatic: Diligent from dusk till dawn, he threads ten thousand hinges.

sentences.zh: 雖治興，匪荒寧。

translations.literal: Though rule flourishes--not abandoned to wasteful ease.
translations.idiomatic: Though order thrives he never sinks into slack peace.

sentences.zh: 謙道樂，沖不盈。

translations.literal: The teaching of modesty delights; the hollow heart never fills.
translations.idiomatic: Humility is his joy; the yielding vessel never brims.

sentences.zh: 天地合德，日月同榮。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth join virtues; sun and moon share splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Earth and sky wed their powers; sun and moon twin their beams.

sentences.zh: 赫赫煌煌，曜幽冥。

translations.literal: Blazing blazing, glorious glorious--shining even through darkness.
translations.idiomatic: Radiance blazes; gloom itself grows bright.

sentences.zh: 三光克從，於顯天，垂景星。

translations.literal: Three luminaries obey him--how manifest heaven--hanging down sight-giving stars.
translations.idiomatic: Sun, moon, and stars obey; bright heaven drops blessing stars.

sentences.zh: 龍鳳臻，甘露宵零。

translations.literal: Dragon and phoenix arrive; sweet dew sprinkles through the night.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon and phoenix gather; midnight nectar sprinkles down.

sentences.zh: 肅神祗，祗上靈。

translations.literal: Revering the spirits--honoring the high numina.
translations.idiomatic: He bows to every god and feeds the highest spirits.

sentences.zh: 萬物欣戴，自天效其成。

translations.literal: All creation rejoices to uphold him; from heaven comes proof of success.
translations.idiomatic: Creation delights to bear him up; heaven itself sends proof of deed.

sentences.zh: 仲春振旅

translations.literal: Second Month Drills the Host
translations.idiomatic: Second Month Drills the Host

sentences.zh: 仲春振旅，大致人，武教於時日新。

translations.literal: Second month drills the host--greatly aligns the people--martial instruction with the seasons daily renewed.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-spring shakes out the army, rallies the people, and keeps martial teaching fresh with each dawn.

sentences.zh: 師執提，工執鼓。

translations.literal: Masters grasp spear-butts; craftsmen grasp drums.
translations.idiomatic: Officers carry spear-hafts; artisans beat the drums.

sentences.zh: 坐作從，節有序。

translations.literal: Sitting and rising follow command; the beat keeps sequence.
translations.idiomatic: They kneel and rise on cue; cadence orders every move.

sentences.zh: 盛矣允文允武！

translations.literal: Splendid indeed--true pattern in civil, true pattern in martial!
translations.idiomatic: Sublime indeed, civil truth and martial truth together!

sentences.zh: 搜田表祃，申法誓。

translations.literal: Hunting in the open they raise the war-prayer; they proclaim statutes and oaths.
translations.idiomatic: They sweep the fields and plant the maoling banner; they declare law and oath.

sentences.zh: 遂圍禁，獻社祭。

translations.literal: Then closing the preserves they offer the soil altar's sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: They ring the chase and present the earth-god offering.

sentences.zh: 允以時，明國制。

translations.literal: Fit for the season--clarifying national regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Timed to season they publish the royal ordinance.

sentences.zh: 文武並用，禮之經。

translations.literal: Civil and martial employed together--ritual's warp-thread.
translations.idiomatic: Culture and arms paired as ritual's warp.

sentences.zh: 列車如戰，大教明，古今誰能去兵？

translations.literal: Chariots arrayed like battle--great instruction clear--who in ancient or modern times can dispense with arms?
translations.idiomatic: Lines of chariots mimic war; the lesson blazes clear: can any age be rid of spears?

sentences.zh: 大晉繼天，濟群生。

translations.literal: Great Jin continues heaven--succors the throng of lives.
translations.idiomatic: Great Jin carries heaven's line and feeds every common life.

sentences.zh: 夏苗田

translations.literal: Summer Seedling Hunt
translations.idiomatic: Summer Seedling Hunt

sentences.zh: 夏苗田，運將徂。

translations.literal: Summer seedling hunt--the march is about to depart.
translations.idiomatic: The summer seedling hunt begins as the column prepares to march.

sentences.zh: 軍國異容，文武殊。

translations.literal: Army and state wear different faces--civil and martial diverge.
translations.idiomatic: Camp and court wear different faces; culture and arms wear different masks.

sentences.zh: 乃命群吏，撰車徒，辯其號名，贊契書。

translations.literal: Thereupon he charges host of officers--assemble chariots and foot--distinguish their callsigns--assist tally-documents.
translations.idiomatic: He bids every clerk ready carts and men, sort each banner-name, and chalk the tallies.

sentences.zh: 王軍啟八門，行同上帝居。

translations.literal: Royal army opens eight gates--march matches supreme lord's dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: The royal host opens eight gates; its march mirrors god's court.

sentences.zh: 時路建大麾，雲旗翳紫虛。

translations.literal: Seasonal road raises great banner--cloud pennons veil purple void.
translations.idiomatic: Battle standards rear along the route; cloud-flags veil the violet sky.

sentences.zh: 百官象其事，疾則疾，徐則徐。

translations.literal: Hundred offices image their tasks--swift where swift, slow where slow.
translations.idiomatic: Each ministry mirrors its charge: hurry where hurry fits, tarry where tarry fits.

sentences.zh: 回衡旋軫，罷陣弊車。

translations.literal: Turning shafts, wheeling axles--dismiss formations, idle chariots.
translations.idiomatic: They swing yoke and axle, break array, and park the cars.

sentences.zh: 獻禽享祀，蒸蒸配有虞。

translations.literal: Presenting quarry at sacrifice--steaming vigor matches Shun's court.
translations.idiomatic: They offer the bag at the altar; steam rises worthy of Shun.

sentences.zh: 惟大晉，德參兩儀，化雲敷。

translations.literal: Only Great Jin--virtue joins two powers--transforming clouds spread.
translations.idiomatic: Great Jin alone marries heaven and earth; clouds of reform roll wide.

sentences.zh: 仲秋獮田

translations.literal: Second Month Autumn Hunt
translations.idiomatic: Second Month Autumn Hunt

sentences.zh: 仲秋獮田，金德常綱。
